name: array-axes-slicing
title: 0-based half-open slices in 1D and axis reductions on a 2D (rows, cols) grid
description: Left panel shows 1D array a = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50]) with 0-based indices 0..4 and negative indices -5..-1, illustrating why half-open slice a[1:4] includes index 1 (20) and excludes stop 4 to return [20, 30, 40] while strided slice a[::2] returns [10, 30, 50]. Right panel shows a 2 by 3 grid [[1, 2, 3], [10, 20, 30]] where axis=0 collapses down rows to per-column shape (3,) [11, 22, 33], axis=1 collapses across columns to per-row shape (2,) [6, 60], and the axis number names the dimension that gets collapsed.

name: array-views
title: A NumPy slice is a view into shared memory; .copy() allocates new memory
description: Starting from original = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40]), assigning view[0] = 99 on view = original[:2] mutates the shared memory buffer so original becomes [99, 20, 30, 40], whereas separate = original[:2].copy() allocates independent memory so separate[0] = -5 leaves original intact.

name: python-environments
title: Lock one project environment and point both kernel and shell at it
description: Three dependency solvers and environment tools — uv solving and locking the PyPI graph via uv sync --frozen --extra teaching, pip + venv resolving against the current environment via python -m pip install, and conda or mamba solving Python plus compiled C and CUDA libraries such as CFITSIO, FFTW and MPI — build an isolated project environment (.venv/bin/python for uv or venv, or .../envs/<project>/bin/python for conda). Two aligned paths — the Python PhD (locked) Jupyter kernel via ipykernel and an activated shell via source activate or uv run — execute inside that project environment, whereas an unactivated shell running bare pip install or pytest hits /usr/bin/python3 or conda (base) and raises ModuleNotFoundError.

name: shared-mask
title: One mask preserves row alignment
description: An illustrative table applies one Boolean row mask to distance, velocity and uncertainty so rows 0 and 3 stay aligned, while contrasting separate per-column masks that both return length 3 and silently pair row 2's 2100 km/s velocity with row 1's 30 km/s error.

name: broadcasting
title: Broadcast M trial slopes against N galaxies, then sum across axis=1
description: Column vector h0_grid[:, None] of shape (M, 1) with M = 201 trial slopes multiplies distance[valid] of shape (N,) treated as (1, N) across N = 395 galaxies plus intercept 300 to form the (M, N) prediction matrix v_model with entries H_i d_j + 300, followed by .sum(axis=1) collapsing across the N galaxy columns into chi2 of shape (M,) with one chi-squared score per trial H0.

name: catalogue-selection
title: Data-hygiene filtering and physical survey selection are separate steps
description: Left-to-right flow from Raw catalogue (400 rows) to Rejected: invalid (5 rows) and Valid catalogue (395 rows), then through magnitude cut m < 16.5 to Selected (262 rows) and Valid, not selected (133 rows), comparing the Valid catalogue (395 reference) and Selected (262) distance distributions on shared distance bins.

name: fits-vs-ecsv
title: ECSV stores space-delimited text + YAML; FITS packs Header/Data Units (HDUs)
description: Side-by-side comparison of Astropy ECSV 1.0 plain-text YAML headers (# %ECSV 1.0, datatype and nested meta dicts above space-delimited text rows) against FITS binary containers (HDU 0 Primary HDU with no data plus HDU 1 Binary Table HDU preserving <=8-character keywords and TUNITn column units while >8-character keys trigger HIERARCH warnings and nested dicts fail).

name: nyquist-aliasing
title: Frequencies above Nyquist fold back into the resolved [0, fs/2] band
description: At a 512 Hz sampling rate with Nyquist limit 256 Hz, a 40 Hz tone stays resolved at 40 Hz, whereas a 300 Hz tone (256 + 44 Hz) folds across the 256 Hz mirror to an alias at 212 Hz (512 - 300 = 256 - 44 Hz) that is indistinguishable at 1/512 s discrete samples.

name: git-states
title: A commit records the staged snapshot
description: A first test-file version is staged, then edited again. Without staging the new edit, the next local commit contains the earlier snapshot.

name: git-branches
title: Resolve two descriptions before the merge commit
description: Two branches change the same README paragraph. Their shared history joins in a merge commit after the conflict is resolved to preserve both units and shortest-arc meaning.

name: git-undo-vs-revert
title: Private reset rewinds the branch pointer; shared revert adds a new inverse commit
description: Two timelines from C1 (good) to C2 (mistake): git reset --soft HEAD~1 rewinds private branch recovery-lab back to C1 while keeping C2's changes staged to fix and recommit, whereas git revert HEAD and git push keep C2 in shared history and add inverse commit C3 so collaborators fast-forward safely.

name: git-remotes
title: Local commits, remote branches and hosted review
description: Push updates hosted branches; fetch updates local remote-tracking references. A pull request compares hosted branches for review. Fetch alone does not edit the working files.

name: agent-architecture
title: Locate the client, model and tool execution
description: On your workstation (for example VS Code or a terminal), the agent client (Claude Code, Codex or Cline) mediates permission-controlled file and terminal tools against local workspace files, while an LLM endpoint (cloud API or local server) only receives context and proposes next steps. An OS shell sandbox is a separate boundary only in tools that provide one.

name: agent-review-loop
title: Keep scientific expectations under human control
description: A student supplies the task and independently justified expectations, reviews an agent plan and derives test cases, reviews the drafted test_student_checks.py, verifies the failing run and commits a fixed tests checkpoint before authorising the weighted_mean.py repair, then reruns independently and inspects the diff before accepting.
